new.title: Walk the Roman town of Cambodunum
new.desc: The Archaeological Park shows the Roman settlement from the time of Emperor Augustus, in three areas: a Gallo-Roman temple district with five reconstructed buildings, the small baths under a museum hall, and the forum with basilica and praetorium. Excavations began in 1885 and the park has been open to the public since 1983.
new.tip: Allow an hour or two and check seasonal opening times first. It lies just east of the Iller, an easy walk from the old town.

new.title: Tour the Rococo state rooms of the Residenz
new.desc: The Prince-Abbots' palace was the first monumental monastery complex built in Germany after the Thirty Years' War, begun in 1651. Its state rooms, finished by 1743 with paintings, sculpture and Wessobrunn stucco, are among the finest Rococo interiors in southern Germany.
new.tip: State rooms are visited on a guided tour only, so check the schedule and book ahead in busy seasons.

new.title: Step inside the Basilica of St. Lorenz
new.desc: The former abbey church of the Prince-Abbey of Kempten stands beside the Residenz and was begun during the Thirty Years' War. It is dedicated to St. Lawrence and to the city's patron saints Gordian and Epimachus, and locals simply call it the St. Lorenz Basilica.
new.tip: Combine it with the Residenz and Hildegardplatz outside. Free to enter, but be quiet during services.

new.title: Climb into the story of St. Mang
new.desc: This Lutheran town church, mostly 15th century, was the centre of the Reformation around Kempten from 1527. It was remodelled in Rococo style in 1767 and given a neo-Gothic look a century later. Its tower gives views over the Rathausplatz and the town hall.
new.tip: Pair it with a stroll round St.-Mang-Platz, where medieval houses and an old churchyard site surround the church.

new.title: Admire the town hall on Rathausplatz
new.desc: Kempten's medieval town hall dates from 1474 and replaced a half-timbered granary of 1368. A 17th-century fountain stands before it, and the current facade comes from the 1930s. The mayor and city council still sit here.
new.tip: Best seen in the morning light with a coffee at one of the cafés on the square.

new.title: Climb the Burghalde for the best view
new.desc: This hill in the old town was settled in late antiquity and held the abbot's castle in the Middle Ages. Since the 19th century it has been Kempten's first citizens' park, with castle ruins, an open-air stage, a scent garden and a castle museum. From the top you see the Alps to the south, the Residenz to the west and the Roman temple district to the east.
new.tip: Go at golden hour. It is a short, steep climb from the old town and free to enter.

new.title: Admire the Baroque Kornhaus
new.desc: This cross-shaped Baroque building by Johann Jakob Herkomer once stored the abbey's grain. Its large hall is used for balls, conferences and theatre, and its cellar vaults housed the winter farmers' market until 1998.
new.tip: Look at the exterior and the square first, then check what is on in the hall.

new.title: Stroll the terraces of the Hofgarten
new.desc: This 3.4 hectare Baroque palace garden lies north of the Residenz and is laid out on terraces of different heights. It is a calm green corner of the old town, and classical concerts are held in the Residenz courtyards nearby.
new.tip: Free and open to all. A good picnic stop after the Residenz tour.

new.title: Browse the Orangerie library
new.desc: The Orangerie closed the north end of the Hofgarten in 1780 as a late Baroque building with Classical touches. Since 1963 it has housed the city library.
new.tip: Walk in from the Hofgarten and admire the building. Check the library's public hours.

new.title: Meet Kempten's past at the Kempten-Museum
new.desc: The Zumsteinhaus was built in 1802 for a merchant family from Savoy. After a long renovation it reopened as the Kempten-Museum in December 2019, replacing the old Roman and natural history museums that had been here.
new.tip: A solid rainy-day stop on Residenzplatz. Check current hours before you go.

new.title: See contemporary art in the old Stiftsmälzerei
new.desc: The Kunsthalle sits in the Stiftsmälzerei, the abbey's 1788 brewhouse and malt house on Memminger Straße, and mainly shows contemporary art. The building was meant to form a trio of abbey service courtyards with the Marstall and Kornhaus.
new.tip: Check the exhibition programme before visiting.

new.title: Find Kempten's oldest church, the Keckkapelle
new.desc: The Chapel of St. Stephen im Keck is of Romanesque origin and is the oldest church in the city. It started as a leper chapel and was rebuilt and extended several times.
new.tip: A quiet detour north of the centre. Often only the exterior is open, so go for the setting.

new.title: Find the Flora-Tempel in the Stadtpark
new.desc: This small octagonal garden pavilion with a mansard roof was built in 1762 for Prince-Abbot Honorius Roth von Schreckenstein. It stood in the Stadtpark until it was moved to its present spot in 1981. The Stadtpark itself was laid out in the 1890s to join the old imperial and abbey towns.
new.tip: A pleasant five minute detour between the old town and the Residenz. Free.

new.title: Spot the medieval houses of the Mühlberg
new.desc: Three staggered late medieval houses stand just north of St. Mang. Renovation work in the winter of 1996/97 uncovered a trove of everyday finds hidden in floor fillings and wall panelling.
new.tip: Walk it with St. Mang. It is an exterior look only.

new.title: Visit Brother Jörg at St. Anton
new.desc: The Capuchin church of St. Anthony in the south of town holds the remains of Brother Jörg (1696 to 1762). They were brought across the Alps from Italy 160 years after his death and rest in a wall niche.
new.tip: Quiet and free. Respect worshippers and visit outside service times.

new.title: Look at the Allgäuhalle, a 1920s cattle hall
new.desc: Built in 1928 as a livestock breeding hall, it was the first facility of its kind in southern Germany. It was meant for cattle but also hosted sport and big events, and was listed as a monument in 2015.
new.tip: Mostly an architecture stop from the outside, near the station. Check events inside.

new.title: Hike up Mariaberg to the city's high point
new.desc: The ridge of Mariaberg rises to 915 m at Höhenegg, the highest point in Kempten. The pilgrimage chapel of Mariä Heimsuchung was built in the village in 1783, and the summit area looks to the Ammergau Alps and the Zugspitze on clear days.
new.tip: Pick a clear day and bring water. A good half-day walk out of town.

new.title: Cross the Iller on the Illersteg footbridge
new.desc: The Illersteg is a pedestrian and cycle bridge over the Iller, the river that shaped Kempten. The long Iller cycle route runs about 146 km from Oberstdorf downstream to Ulm, so this is a handy place to join it.
new.tip: Walk the river banks on both sides, then climb to the old town. Free.

new.title: Walk around the Stadtweiher pond
new.desc: The Stadtweiher is an old pond on the edge of the Stiftallmey district, on the road toward Buchenberg. It is one of the artificial ponds in Kempten that are several hundred years old.
new.tip: A quiet green loop west of the centre. Good with kids. Free.

new.title: Relax in the Calgeerpark
new.desc: This park was laid out in 1909 by city gardener Dominikus Senn, financed by the merchant and benefactor Christian Marco Calgèer. It shrank over time through later building, but remains a calm green space between Adenauerring and Parkstraße.
new.tip: A short rest stop in the city centre. Free.

new.title: Wander the Haubenschloss park
new.desc: The Haubenschloss is a listed rectangular building on the grounds of an old Gothic manor, Anwanden. Its park was laid out by city gardener Dominikus Senn before the First World War.
new.tip: Good for a relaxed walk south of the centre. Free.

new.title: Eat Krustenbraten at Zum Stift
new.desc: This neo-Baroque brewery inn of 1906, with its oriel tower and curved gable, stands next to the old abbey brewhouse. Reviewers praise the pork roast with dark beer sauce, as well as Kaiserschmarrn and apple strudel.
new.tip: Sit in the beer garden or main room and order the Krustenbraten. Check current hours.

new.title: Drink a Meckatzer at the Bräu-Engel
new.desc: This inn on Prälat-Götz-Straße has been a pub since at least 1819 and has belonged to the Meckatzer brewery since 1934. It was fully renovated in 1997 and is one of Kempten's classic Wirtshäuser.
new.tip: Order a Meckatzer beer with a Swabian dish. Check opening days first.

new.title: Sip wine at the Goldenes Fässle
new.desc: The building at Promenadestraße 2 was the oldest pure wine bar in Kempten. After a restoration it reopened in December 2018 as the Goldenes Fässle.
new.tip: Go for a glass of wine in the evening. Check current opening hours.

new.title: Hang out at the Künstlerhaus café
new.desc: This 1873 villa is a café, restaurant, small stage and cultural meeting place. Guests report large portions and a beer garden.
new.tip: Check the stage calendar for a night with music or comedy.

new.title: Take coffee on the Klostersteige
new.desc: Caffè Baffetti has a large outdoor seating area in the pedestrian zone at Klostersteige 7 and is rated highly by local reviewers.
new.tip: Perfect for an espresso stop between Rathausplatz and the Residenz.

new.title: Smell fresh roast at Weber Rösterei
new.desc: A coffee roastery and shop right on Rathausplatz 13, listed among Kempten's coffee addresses.
new.tip: Pick up beans to take home. Check opening hours first.

new.title: Get coffee in the Engelhaldepark
new.desc: The Engelhalde landscape park was created by reclaiming a gravel pit, and Café Engelhaldepark sits at Lohmühltobel 1, with food and burger nights reported by reviewers.
new.tip: Combine with a walk through the park. Check opening days.

new.title: Settle in at the Schalander
new.desc: A mid-range restaurant at Fischersteige 9 in the middle of the old town, listed by Wikivoyage among Kempten's places to eat.
new.tip: Book ahead for dinner and check the menu online.

new.title: Shop the Hildegardplatz weekly market
new.desc: The weekly market is held on Hildegardplatz beside the basilica on Wednesdays and Saturdays. It is the place for local cheese, bread and produce.
new.tip: Go on a Saturday morning for the best choice and ask for Allgäuer Bergkäse.

new.title: Walk through the Breitachklamm gorge
new.desc: The Breitachklamm is the deepest rock gorge in central Europe, with a 2.5 km footpath that about 300,000 people walk each year. It is closed for several weeks in spring and autumn for rock clearing and repairs.
new.tip: Check that the gorge is open. Take a jacket, because it is cold and damp inside.

new.title: Ride the Nebelhorn cable car
new.desc: The three-section Nebelhornbahn rises about 1400 m over 5.7 km. It was built between 1928 and 1930, and the lower stretches were fully replaced in 2021. The 2224 m summit looks far over the Alps.
new.tip: Pick a clear day and go early. Check the weather webcam before buying a ticket.

new.title: Ride the Fellhornbahn to the alpenrose meadows
new.desc: The Fellhorn is 2037 m high, is reached by the Fellhornbahn cable car from the Birgsau valley, sits on the German and Austrian border, and is famed for its large fields of alpenroses. It is one of the Allgäu's classic flower mountains.
new.tip: Go in early summer for the blooms. The cable car starts in the Birgsau valley.

new.title: Stand under the Heini-Klopfer ski flying hill
new.desc: This huge ski flying hill has a hill size of 235 m and a record of 242.5 m, making it one of the largest in the world. The free-cantilevered concrete tower is nicknamed the leaning tower of Oberstdorf.
new.tip: It sits next to the Freibergsee, so combine the two. Check visitor access in summer.

new.title: Hike the Oytal to the Stuibenfall
new.desc: The Oytal is a side valley running east from the Trettach valley. A walk up from the Oytalhaus passes the Stuibenfall waterfall, about 25 m high, in around an hour. Beyond it lies the Käseralpe.
new.tip: Bring sturdy shoes. The road up the valley is closed to most traffic, so walk, bike or ride a carriage.

new.title: Stand where the Iller begins
new.desc: Three Alpine rivers, the Breitach, Stillach and Trettach, join near Oberstdorf to form the Iller. The Iller cycle route starts here and runs 146 km to Ulm.
new.tip: A good start for a bike ride along the river. Free.

new.title: Wade the Starzlachklamm gorge
new.desc: The gorge at the foot of the Grünten has foaming pools, giant potholes, a rock roof and a 12 m waterfall. It is a protected natural monument and rated a valuable geotope.
new.tip: Wear sturdy shoes and take it slowly on wet rock. Check seasonal opening.

new.title: Look up at the Grünten, guardian of the Allgäu
new.desc: The Grünten is a 1738 m ridge right on the edge of the Alps, nicknamed Wächter des Allgäus. Its summit carries a mountain-troops memorial and a broadcasting tower, and a cable car and two huts serve the slopes.
new.tip: Check the lift status or hike up. Views over the plain are best on a clear day.

new.title: Circle the Großer Alpsee lake
new.desc: The Große Alpsee is a natural lake of nearly 250 ha with an 8.1 km shore, west of Immenstadt in the northern Allgäu Alps.
new.tip: Walk or bike the shore path and bring a swimsuit in summer.

new.title: Descend into the Sturmannshöhle cave
new.desc: This karst cave near Obermaiselstein is 460 m long and is the only show cave in the region. The entrance lies at 978 m and is reached by stairs.
new.tip: It stays cool inside, so wear a jacket. A good rainy-day pick.

new.title: Ride up to the Hochgrat on the Nagelfluhkette
new.desc: The Hochgrat is 1834 m and is the highest peak of the Nagelfluhkette, a ridge of conglomerate rock and part of a nature park. It is the home mountain of Oberstaufen and is served by the Hochgratbahn.
new.tip: Go on a clear day and check the lift times. Strong hikers can follow the ridge.

new.title: Follow the Eistobel gorge
new.desc: The Eistobel is a gorge of the Obere Argen with cliffs up to 130 m, where the river drops about 70 m in cascades over roughly 3 km. Its name comes from winters when the waterfalls froze solid for months.
new.tip: Wear grippy shoes and stay on marked paths.

new.title: Walk the treetops at skywalk allgäu
new.desc: This 6 hectare nature park near Scheidegg has a tree-top path as its main attraction, plus a barefoot trail, adventure paths and a skills course. It opened in October 2010 and is barrier-free.
new.tip: Fine for families. Check opening times and tickets online.

new.title: See the Altes Rathaus on Lindau island
new.desc: The Old Town Hall on Lindau island was built between 1422 and 1436 and is one of the island's best known buildings.
new.tip: Wander the harbour and Maximilianstraße around it. Free to see.

new.title: Climb the Lindau lighthouse
new.desc: The Lindau lighthouse is the only lighthouse in Bavaria, 36 m high, with a clock in its facade. It stands guard at the harbour entrance, and the lion statue nearby is the other landmark of the Lake Constance harbour.
new.tip: Go at sunset. Check the hours for climbing the tower.

new.title: Find the Siebendächerhaus in Memmingen
new.desc: This former tanner's house, with seven stacked roofs, is one of Memmingen's seven landmarks.
new.tip: Combine it with the Stadtbach lanes and Weber am Bach nearby. Free.

new.title: Stand on Memmingen's Marktplatz
new.desc: The town hall is a multi-storey Renaissance building of the 16th century that closes the Marktplatz to the northeast and is one of Memmingen's most famous buildings.
new.tip: Sit on the square and look up. Free.

new.title: Marvel at the Ottobeuren Basilica
new.desc: The abbey church of St. Alexander and Theodor is a high point of the Upper Swabian Baroque Road. It became a basilica minor in 1926 and is known for its concerts.
new.tip: Go for the interior. Check opening and concert dates.

new.title: Climb to the Hohes Schloss in Bad Grönenbach
new.desc: The Hohes Schloss is the landmark of the Kneipp spa town, standing on a steep conglomerate rock at the western edge of the village.
new.tip: Combine with a stroll in the Kneipp resort. Check castle access.

new.title: Stroll Isny's old town and Wassertor
new.desc: Isny kept the look of a medieval imperial city. The Wassertor tower was the northern main gate, and now houses a small museum about the watchman and prisoners.
new.tip: Pair it with the Nikolaikirche. Check museum hours.

new.title: Pass through the Martinstor in Wangen
new.desc: This five-storey gate, first mentioned in 1347, was reshaped in 1608 and painted in 1924. It is one of three surviving gates of Wangen's old town.
new.tip: Walk the Paradiesstraße to the Frauentor too. Free.

new.title: Eat at the Oytalhaus in the mountains
new.desc: The Gasthof Oytal at about 1,010 m is the walkers' stop in the Oytal, with huts on the Untere Gutenalp and the Käseralpe higher up in summer.
new.tip: Walk up from Oberstdorf, eat a Brotzeit, and ask about opening dates.

new.title: Taste organic cheese at Hofgut Ratzenberg
new.desc: This estate in Lindenberg combines an organic farm dairy, a farm restaurant and a farm shop, and runs a cheese school for groups. It is on the Westallgäuer cheese route.
new.tip: Check which days the restaurant and shop open.
new.q: Hofgut Ratzenberg, Sedanstraße 55, Lindenberg im Allgäu

new.title: Buy mountain cheese at the Bergkäserei Steibis
new.desc: This mountain dairy in Steibis lets visitors look behind the scenes. Visitors mention Obazda, wild herb cheese and cured meats.
new.tip: Pick up Bergkäse for a picnic. Check dairy hours.
new.q: Bergkäserei Steibis, Im Dorf, Steibis, Oberstaufen

new.title: Eat bread at Wangen's Fidelisbäck
new.desc: A bakery with its own inn on Paradiesstraße. Its history goes back to 1505, which makes it one of the oldest bakeries still operating. The colourful facade paintings are a sight too.
new.tip: Stop for a pastry after walking the Wangen old town.

new.title: Drink a Stolz beer in Isny
new.desc: Brauerei Stolz is a private brewery in Isny im Allgäu, founded in 1919.
new.tip: Order a Stolz beer in an Isny pub after a walk in the old town.

new.title: Dine by the stream at Weber am Bach
new.desc: The tourism office describes this wine bar and restaurant in Memmingen as old and traditional, with outdoor seating right on the Stadtbach. The house was a Latin school until 1572 and had its first wine bar in 1848.
new.tip: Reserve a table on the terrace in summer.
new.q: Weber am Bach, Untere Bachgasse 2, Memmingen

new.title: Warm up in the Blaue Traube Stüberl
new.desc: This Memmingen Gasthaus in a 16th and 17th century building has a traditionally furnished Stüberl and a wine bar.
new.tip: Try it for a cosy evening in the old town. Check hours.

new.title: Seek out the Meckatzer brewery in Heimenkirch
new.desc: Meckatzer Löwenbräu is a brewery in the hamlet of Meckatz in Heimenkirch in the Westallgäu. The same house owns the Bräu-Engel pub in Kempten.
new.tip: Combine with a drive through the Westallgäu hills. Check for brewery tours.

new.title: Taste the Zötler beer of the Allgäu
new.desc: Privat-Brauerei Zötler in Rettenberg produces about 88,500 hl of beer a year and has brewed the Allgäuer Festwoche beer since 2010.
new.tip: Look for Zötler on menus across the Allgäu.
